name: auth
description: Identity, capabilities and delegation: who you are, what you may do, and how to grant bounded authority to others via UCAN tokens. Load when permissions matter.

content.inline:
## Auth & capabilities
Identity is a DID; every job records its caller. `v/ops/auth/whoami` returns yours.

`v/ops/auth/identity-token` saves a bearer for your exact caller identity as a secret: `{aud: <target venue DID>, name: <secret name>, lifetime: 300}`. Works only for the venue signing key DID and identities nested beneath it, including agents. Requires secret/write on s/<name>; generic invocation additionally requires invoke on the operation reference; agents use their owner's secret store. Returns `{secret, sub, aud, exp}`, never the bearer or key. Use the secret reference with secret/use authority. Lifetime is 1..3600 seconds; refresh with overwrite:true before expiry. This token grants NO permissions and does not admit an agent as a native user.

Capabilities are `{with, can}` pairs: `with` is a resource (a path prefix like `w/reports/`, a DID URL, or a scheme resource); `can` is an ability. Core abilities: `crud/read`, `crud/write`, `asset/read`, `asset/store`, `invoke` (the right to look up and run an arbitrary operation at a permitted location; bound tools need no invoke grant and still enforce resource authority), `secret/use` (send a secret's value without seeing it; a grant may carry `nb: {url: <prefix>}` to bind it to one destination), plus adapter-specific ones (`mcp/manage`, `sql/query`...). Enforcement happens at each operation's own enforcement point — a denial reads `Capability denied` and names the resource.

An agent acts with its controller's authority narrowed by its current config.caps. Presented UCANs add rights, but cannot escape access-token or callable caps. A gate constrains only its own grant; an unconditional covering grant can still authorise. Anonymous access follows venue policy: off, explicitly configured, or read-only by default (own-namespace crud/read plus asset/read).

Outbound HTTP requires outbound/http/<method> on <ownerDID>/outbound, including model APIs, MCP and bound tools. nb.url restricts the actual destination. Configured model calls use harness/controller authority and grant no outbound permission to the agent itself. admin/outbound/bypass on <venueDID>/outbound bypasses address policy only; the old outbound/any ability is no longer used.

Delegation (UCAN):
- issue `{aud, att, exp}` — a venue-signed token granting the audience DID the attenuated capabilities `att` (an array of `{with, can}`) until `exp`. Grant the MINIMUM: narrow resources, short expiry.
- verify `{token, with?, can?, aud?}` checks a presented token.
- Callers present tokens in the request envelope (`ucans`); cross-user reads then verify against them.

Loading a skill never grants authority — its tools are still checked against all capabilities available for that invocation.
